<div>
    <ul>
    <li><strong>response_status</strong>:  Indicates whether the request was successful or not (success / failed).</li>
    <li><strong>message</strong>: Error message in case of failure.</li>
    <li><strong>data:</strong></li>
    
    <li><strong>id</strong>: The unique identifier for the payment transaction.</li>
    <li><strong>type</strong>: The type of transaction, in this case,("Deposit" or "Card").</li>
    <li><strong>currency</strong>: The currency used for the transaction, (USD).</li>
    <li><strong>total_amount</strong>: The total amount of the transaction.</li>
    <li><strong>total_fees</strong>: The total fees applied to the transaction.</li>
    <li><strong>total_service_tax</strong>: The total service tax applied to the transaction.</li>
    <li><strong>total_added_tax</strong>: The total added tax applied to the transaction.</li>
    <li><strong>original_amount</strong>: The original amount of the transaction.</li>
    <li><strong>buyer_payed_amount</strong>: The amount paid by the buyer.</li>
    <li><strong>buyer_total_fees</strong>:<code>buyer_service_tax</code> + <code>buyer_added_tax</code> The total fees paid by the buyer.</li>
    <li><strong>buyer_service_tax</strong>: The service tax paid by the buyer.</li>
    <li><strong>buyer_added_tax</strong>: The added tax paid by the buyer.</li>
    <li><strong>buyer_fees_map</strong>: A map of fees paid by the buyer.</li>
    <li><strong>seller_received_amount</strong>: The amount received by the seller.</li>
    <li><strong>seller_total_fees</strong>: <code>seller_service_tax</code> + <code>seller_added_tax</code> The total fees for the seller.</li>
    <li><strong>seller_service_tax</strong>: The service tax for the seller.</li>
    <li><strong>seller_added_tax</strong>: The added tax for the seller.</li>
    <li><strong>seller_fees_map</strong>: A map of fees for the seller.</li>
    <li><strong>seller_public_key</strong>: The public key of the seller.</li>
    <li><strong>date</strong>: The date and time of the transaction.</li>
    <li><strong>notes</strong>: Any additional notes or comments regarding the transaction.</li>
    <li><strong>status</strong>: The status of the transaction, which can be one of the following:
        <ul>
            <li>Completed</li>
            <li>Pending</li>
            <li>Refused</li>
            <li>Waiting a Holding Time</li>
            <li>Need Our Review</li>
            <li>Not Paid</li>
            <li>Canceled</li>
            <li>Refunded</li>
            <li>Test Payment</li>
        </ul>
    </li>
    <li><strong>status_tag</strong>: The status tag of the transaction, represented by one of the following codes:
        <ul>
            <li>A</li>
            <li>B</li>
            <li>C</li>
            <li>D</li>
            <li>E</li>
            <li>F</li>
            <li>G</li>
            <li>H</li>
            <li>T</li>
        </ul>
    </li>
</ul>

</div>
<div>
    <p>This relationship illustrates the correspondence between the transaction status and its corresponding tag. Each specific transaction status is assigned a tag for easy reference and efficient processing. Through this relationship, programmers or systems can quickly identify the transaction status by checking its corresponding tag.</p>
</div>
<div>
   <ul>
   
    <li><strong>Status:</strong> Completed → <strong>Tag:</strong> A : Payment completed and amount transferred to the seller.</li>
    <li><strong>Status:</strong> Pending → <strong>Tag:</strong> B : Payment added to seller's pending balance, awaiting delivery of service.</li>
    <li><strong>Status:</strong> Refused → <strong>Tag:</strong> C : Payment refused. Transaction did not go through.</li>
    <li><strong>Status:</strong> Waiting a Holding Time → <strong>Tag:</strong> D : Payment waiting for holding time, but added to seller's pending balance. May be released after a specified period.</li>
    <li><strong>Status:</strong> Need Our Review → <strong>Tag:</strong> E : Payment needs our review, but amount added to seller's pending balance. Pending approval.</li>
    <li><strong>Status:</strong> Not Paid → <strong>Tag:</strong> F : Payment not completed. This is only a deposit; no funds have been transferred.</li>
    <li><strong>Status:</strong> Canceled → <strong>Tag:</strong> G : Payment canceled by either buyer or seller before completion.</li>
    <li><strong>Status:</strong> Refunded → <strong>Tag:</strong> H : Payment refunded to the buyer.</li>
    <li><strong>Status:</strong> Test Payment → <strong>Tag:</strong> T : Test payment, not involving real funds. Used for testing purposes only.</li>
    <li><strong>Note:</strong> You can accept payments with status A, B, D, or E.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

            <div class="headline">
                Callback 
            </div>
           <div class="title_first">Handling Spaceremit Payment Callbacks: Reacting to Payment Status Changes</div>
           <div>
               Spaceremit sends callbacks to websites by making HTTP POST requests to the specified endpoint URL provided by the customer <a style="margin: 1px;" href="/spaceseller" class="sp_link" target="_blank">Websites And Keys</a>. When a payment status changes or a payment is completed, Spaceremit sends a JSON payload containing relevant information about the payment to the customer's endpoint URL.
               To receive Spaceremit callbacks, customers should implement an endpoint on their server to handle incoming POST requests. This endpoint should be able to parse the JSON payload sent by Spaceremit, verify its authenticity <a style="margin: 1px;" href="#" onclick="side_button_select('content4',1)" class="sp_link">Payment Authentication</a>, and process the payment information accordingly. Once the payment data is received and processed, the customer's server can perform any necessary actions, such as updating the payment status in their database or triggering notifications to users.
           </div>

           <div>
                The JSON callback structure is same as payment authentication JSON response, includes information about the payment transaction.Websites can parse this JSON payload to handle payment authentication and update their systems accordingly.

         <div><p class="title_first" style="font-size: 15px;margin-top: 18px;">Steps for Adding Websites:</p><ol><li>Log in to your Spaceremit account.</li><li>Navigate to the <a href="/spaceseller" class="sp_link" target="_blank">Websites And Keys</a> section and add a new website.</li><li>Within the same page for adding websites, locate the API section. Here, you'll find two sets of codes: Public Key and Secret Key, as well as Test Public Key and Test Secret Key.</li><li>You can utilize the test keys for testing and integration before switching to live keys.</li><li>The test transactions will be visible on the same page.</li></ol></div>

        <div class="one_content" id="content7">
            <div class="headline">
                Security Measures
            </div>
           <div class="title_first">Protecting Customer Card Data And Advanced Security Measures</div>
           <div>
               
At Spaceremit, we understand the critical importance of safeguarding your website's integrity and your customers' sensitive card information. That's why we've implemented a comprehensive suite of advanced security measures designed to fortify the protection of card data throughout every stage of the transaction process.<p></p><p>Central to our security framework is the use of encryption protocols that encrypt customer card details before they are transmitted over the network. By employing industry-standard encryption algorithms, we ensure that sensitive information is transformed into unreadable ciphertext, thereby rendering it virtually impenetrable to unauthorized access or interception. This encryption process not only secures data during transmission but also ensures that it remains protected within our systems, guarding against potential breaches or data compromises.</p><p>Moreover, Spaceremit adheres to stringent security standards and compliance requirements to uphold the highest levels of data protection. Our systems are continuously monitored and audited to identify and address any vulnerabilities or potential security risks proactively. We also implement robust access controls and authentication mechanisms to restrict unauthorized access to sensitive data, further bolstering the security posture of our platform.</p><p>In addition to encryption and access controls, Spaceremit employs cutting-edge technologies and practices to enhance the overall security of your customers' card data. Our infrastructure is designed with redundancy and failover mechanisms to ensure continuous availability and resilience against potential threats or disruptions. Furthermore, we employ real-time monitoring and anomaly detection systems to promptly identify and mitigate any suspicious activities or unauthorized access attempts.</p><p>By prioritizing security, Spaceremit provides you with the confidence and assurance that your customers' card data is protected with the utmost care and diligence. With our advanced security measures in place, you can rest assured that transactions conducted through our platform are conducted in a secure and trustworthy environment, preserving the confidentiality and integrity of your customers' sensitive information.</p></div>
